content.content: When invoked as `deccy new`, the form's flags are recognized in any order: `-m <summary>` is recognized whether it precedes, follows or interleaves with the repeated `--on <id>` and `--evaluates <id>` flags, and an occurrence of either repeated flag is recognized wherever it sits among the occurrences of the other kind.
content.rationale: The form names flags, not positions — D12 fixes what the invocation carries, not the spelling order it carries them in. Fixing recognition as order-free keeps invocations that name the same parts equivalent, and keeps the verb from imposing a spelling no parent fixed. The extended form's surface is the same surface with one more flag on it, so `--evaluates` is recognized under the same order-free rule rather than a second one, and occurrences of the two repeated kinds are left to interleave because no parent groups them and grouping would make recognition turn on where an occurrence sits.
